ideas.description: Exploit: the second step of the early-trim dose curve. E061 removed 12 steps from the 20 px phase for −3.0% time at −0.02 pp on 40 fresh draws. On the E061 tip (225 steps; 20/24/28/32 px at about 59/24/71/71 steps), remove 12 more steps from the 20 px phase only (225 → 213; 20 px about 47 steps). The 24, 28 and 32 px phases keep their exact absolute step counts. The whitening detach, the group-1 freeze (last absolute steps) and the group-2 freeze (last absolute steps) keep the same absolute positions. The LR triangle and Lookahead ramp stretch to the new total as fractions, as in E041/E061. No new shapes; error_on_recompile stays on. Judge on 2 fresh builds × seeds 33–52 (40 draws) against E061's 40 draws, then apply the frozen gate (μ̂ − 1.64·σ_tot ≥ 0.75 and seeds 0–2 ≥ 0.753 on the single committed build, no rebuilds). Record per-step CUDA-event time. This settles W6's crux: do early 20 px steps stay nearly free beyond 225?
ideas.expected: Time about −0.15 s (12 × ~13 ms), to about 4.86–4.90 s (−3%). 40-draw mean −0.20 to +0.02 pp vs E061 (median −0.07). A loss of ≤0.15 pp beats the 0.77 s/pp dial and makes this the tip if the gate passes. Caveat: the population may land near 0.7525, where a single committed build passes the local 0.753 bar only ~40% of the time. A loss of ≥0.2 pp means the warm-up now gets too compressed and the early-trim dial stops at 225.

ideas.description: Exploit, re-pricing the width axis at the new dial. Width cuts were rejected at the old ~1.5 s/pp dial: E010 576→512 gave ~1.4 s/pp, and E021 group 2 gave ~1.0 s/pp on possibly selection-biased seeds. Both beat the re-measured post-freeze dial of 0.77 s/pp (E059). Group 3 is the only group that trains on every step, frozen phases included, so its share of time has grown since E010. On the E061 tip, narrow only group 3 from 512 to 448 channels (a multiple of 64, so tiles stay aligned). Group 3's conv1 becomes 384→448, conv2/3 448→448, and the head takes 448 inputs. Muon lr/wd, schedules, freezes, detach, resolution and Lookahead stay unchanged. The init RNG draw order changes, which is a seed re-draw; the 40 draws absorb it. Recapture every resolution and step variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Record per-step CUDA-event time per phase. Judge on 2 fresh builds × seeds 33–52 against E061's 40 draws. Decision variable: the rate Δtime/Δacc against 0.77 s/pp. Above ~1.0 s/pp, follow up with narrowing plus a +0.25-epoch top-up; that pairing has a positive net value.
ideas.expected: About −1.1 ms per 32 px full step (conv MACs: g3.conv1 ×0.875, conv2/3 ×0.77) and a larger relative cut in the frozen steps. Time −2.5 to −4% (about −0.12 to −0.20 s), to about 4.82–4.90 s. 40-draw mean −0.30 to 0 pp (median −0.13). A rate of ≥1.0 s/pp supports re-opening H2.5 at the new dial. A rate of ≤0.7 s/pp, or a loss of ≥0.3 pp, means 100-way late capacity is binding and width cuts stay closed.

ideas.description: Explore, re-priced: an open Lvl3 that was dropped as I034 when the break-even rate was ~1.5 s/pp. At 0.77 s/pp the break-even loss for a ~0.2 s cut is ~0.26 pp. airbench94 uses 2 convs per group, while this airbench96-style port uses 3. On the E061 tip, remove only the third conv of group 1 (128→128 at 15×15, with its BN-GELU), keeping the residual add and the pool structure otherwise intact. Group-1 conv2/3 cost ~1.9 ms fwd+bwd each per full 32 px step, plus memory-bound BN/GELU on 128×15×15, and they run unfrozen for 75% of steps. The group-1 freeze, whitening detach, group-2 freeze, schedules and Lookahead stay unchanged. Recapture every variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on 2 fresh builds × seeds 33–52 against E061's 40 draws. Record per-step time per phase.
ideas.expected: Time −3.5 to −5% (about −0.18 to −0.25 s), to about 4.77–4.85 s. 40-draw mean −0.45 to −0.05 pp (median −0.2). It beats the dial if the loss is ≤ saving/0.77 (≈0.25–0.3 pp). Then pair it with a +0.25-epoch top-up for a net cut of ~0.1 s at equal accuracy. A loss of ≥0.4 pp means early depth carries the 100-way features and closes H2.5's depth branch.

ideas.description: Re-test, on unbiased seeds, a near-miss rejected on selection-biased ones. E040 (24 px bridge → 20 px) read −0.28 pp on seeds 3–12 right after those seeds selected E036. E041 read −0.20 on the same biased set, yet its successor E061 measured −0.02 pp on fresh seeds. The H4.4 bias (~0.2 pp) therefore explains most of E040's deficit. On the E061 tip, run the 24 px phase's ~24 steps at 20 px instead (20/28/32 px; the 28 and 32 px phases keep their exact absolute step counts and positions). The LR triangle, Lookahead, detach and freeze schedules are unchanged. The 20 px variants are already captured; the 24 px graphs can be dropped from build. error_on_recompile stays on. Judge on 2 fresh builds × seeds 33–52 against E061's 40 draws, then the frozen gate. Run it after the early-trim dose idea so the two early-phase cuts are judged single-factor. If both pass, stack them in a later idea.
ideas.expected: Time −0.09 to −0.12 s (about −2%; E040 measured −2.2%), to about 4.90–4.93 s. 40-draw mean −0.20 to 0 pp (median −0.08). A loss of ≤0.12 pp beats the dial and supports H2.3.8. A loss of ≥0.18 pp confirms that the 20→28 px jump is too large on fresh seeds and closes the early-resolution dial at 20/24/28/32.

ideas.description: Explore, a time-neutral booster on an axis never tested on unbiased seeds. LS was 'flat' between 0.2 and 0.3 only at 3-seed power (E013). E032's −0.23 pp for LS → 0 late came on seeds 3–12 right after they selected E027, the same H4.4 pattern that inflated E040 and E041. Hiverge uses LS ~0.09. On the E061 tip, change only label smoothing from 0.3 to 0.15 in every phase (a midpoint toward Hiverge, less risky than 0.1 for a 100-way head). Pass LS as a constant in the compiled loss and recapture every variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Nothing else changes. Judge on 2 fresh builds × seeds 33–52 against E061's 40 draws. A gain is worth ~0.12 s per 0.15 pp at the dial and can be cashed in by the early-trim ideas.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). 40-draw mean −0.25 to +0.20 pp (median −0.03). A gain of ≥0.12 pp supports H1.5.5 and funds one more 12-step early trim. A loss of ≥0.12 pp shows LS 0.3 regularizes the Lookahead average, which closes LS tuning and with it the last cheap scalar booster.

drop.reason: Superseded and low value. E061 showed that removing 12 early 20 px steps outright costs only −0.02 pp on fresh seeds, and the early-trim dose idea tests the 'early steps are nearly free' question more directly. Merging early batches at fixed data passes saves only per-step overhead (~5% of step time, E011/E047), about 0.05 s, which is below break-even for any measurable loss. The committee forecast 0/4 improve votes. The idea also still targets the E049 tip rather than E061.

The new ideas are built around the re-measured epoch dial: buying accuracy back with more epochs now costs about 0.77 s per percentage point (pp) of accuracy (E059). That makes two things worth revisiting: cuts rejected at the old ~1.5 s/pp rate, and near-misses that were judged on seed sets already reused for earlier keep decisions (H4.4). The tip is E061: 5.02 s, with a pooled 40-draw mean of about 0.7532. A single committed build passes the local 0.753 bar only about half the time, so every candidate goes through the frozen gate.

**Queue after this round:** I096 (Muon → SGD, running), I097 (cheaper GELU, gated) and five new ideas.

**New ideas, highest priority first:**
1. **Second early trim (H4.2.5, priority 5).** Remove 12 more steps from the 20 px phase (225 → 213), about −0.15 s. This answers W6's crux: do early steps stay nearly free beyond 225?
2. **Narrow group 3 from 512 to 448 channels (H2.5, priority 4).** Group 3 is the only group that trains on every step, frozen phases included. The old width results (E010 at ~1.4 s/pp, E021 at ~1.0 s/pp) both beat the new dial. The measured s/pp rate decides whether width cuts reopen, followed by a narrowing-plus-top-up run.
3. **Drop group 1's third conv (H2.5.2, priority 3).** This was dropped as I034 when the break-even rate was 1.5 s/pp. At 0.77 s/pp, a ~0.2 s cut breaks even at a loss of about 0.26 pp.
4. **Drop the 24 px bridge, re-tested on fresh seeds (H2.3.8, priority 3).** E040's −0.28 pp was read on biased seeds, the same pattern that made E041 look bad before E061 came in at −0.02 pp.
5. **Label smoothing 0.3 → 0.15 (H1.5.5, priority 2).** A time-neutral booster on an axis never tested on unbiased seeds.

The mix is roughly two-thirds exploit (ideas 1, 2 and 4) and one-third explore (3 and 5). All are judged on 2 builds × seeds 33–52 against E061.

**Dropped:** I098 (larger early batch). E061 already settles most of its question, and its saving is capped by per-step overhead at about 0.05 s.

**Caveats:**
- Seeds 33–52 have now driven two keeps (E060, E061). Rotate to fresh seeds 73–92 after about three more decisions.
- Run the bridge test after the dose test, so each early-phase cut is judged on its own before stacking.
